I see. So optional blocks are only disabled if something fails to resolve inside them (SEPOL_ENOENT). If everything resolves fine, the optional stays enabled. The `CIL_PASS_BLKIN_LINK` and `CIL_PASS_BLKIN_COPY` passes happen before `CIL_PASS_MISC1` where optional disabling might occur.

Now let me understand the tree structure better. When we have:
```
(block foo
    (optional opt
        (blockinherit foo)))
```

The AST tree would be:
- root (CIL_ROOT)
  - block foo (CIL_BLOCK)
    - optional opt (CIL_OPTIONAL)
      - blockinherit foo (CIL_BLOCKINHERIT)

When `cil_resolve_blockinherit_link` processes the blockinherit node, it resolves `foo` and adds the blockinherit node to `foo->bi_nodes`.

Then in `CIL_PASS_BLKIN_COPY`, when processing block `foo`, it iterates `foo->bi_nodes` and calls `cil_check_recursive_blockinherit` on the blockinherit node. Walking up from the blockinherit node:
- parent = optional opt (CIL_OPTIONAL) - skip (not CIL_BLOCK)
- parent = block foo (CIL_BLOCK) - matches bi->block
- Call `cil_print_recursive_blockinherit(bi_node, block_foo_node)`

In `cil_print_recursive_blockinherit`:
- Walk from bi_node (blockinherit) up to block_foo_node:
  - curr = blockinherit foo (CIL_BLOCKINHERIT): not CIL_BLOCK, curr == bi_node so just prepend curr
  - curr = optional opt (CIL_OPTIONAL): not CIL_BLOCK, curr != bi_node, so prepend `NODE(((struct cil_blockinherit *)curr->data)->block)` - BUG! `curr->data` is `struct cil_optional *`, reading `->block` reads `datum.name` (first field), then `NODE(name)` treats the name string as a `struct cil_symtab_datum *` and reads `->nodes->head->data` at `name + 16` → OOB read
  - curr = block foo (CIL_BLOCK): prepend
